source.title: Generalization for multiclass classification with overparameterized linear models
source.authors: Vignesh Subramanian; Rahul Arya; Anant Sahai

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting the relevant result.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analytically studies generalization of minimum-norm interpolating classifiers in an overparameterized linear model with Gaussian features, and provides asymptotic sufficient conditions and a class-count comparison. This is a conceptual test of overparameterized generalization, not the deep-network experiments in the versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports one main theorem for noiseless labels defined by the largest of k Gaussian features, plus stated comparisons with the binary-classification and regression settings. Results cited from other studies are not recorded as rows. The theorem gives sufficient conditions, not a measured sweep or a converse showing failure outside the region.
record.test_reason: The study proves generalization conditions for minimum-norm linear classifiers with weighted Gaussian features. It does not test random-label memorization alongside natural-label generalization (V1), or whether widening an interpolating neural network keeps lowering test error (V2). Its own results address none of V3–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors prove sufficient conditions for vanishing multiclass classification error in a bi-level Gaussian-feature linear model, explain the difficulty introduced by fewer positive examples per class, and conjecture broader necessary and sufficient conditions. They do not prove failure outside the sufficient region.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes minimum-norm interpolation in a synthetic Gaussian-feature linear model with noiseless multiclass labels and feature weighting. It does not use the deep networks, random-label fitting, or experimental recipes in V1–V8.
record.method_sensitivity: The sufficient generalization region depends on the scaling parameters p, q, r, and t; the paper identifies class growth and the number of favored features as consequential. It also describes an alternative scaling that holds positive examples per class fixed (Appendix G).

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 5.1 proves that multiclass minimum-norm interpolation has misclassification probability tending to zero within a sufficient parameter region of the bi-level Gaussian-feature model, including regimes where prior work establishes regression failure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Minimum-norm interpolating linear multiclass classifiers can generalize asymptotically under suitable feature weighting and joint feature, sample and class scaling.

fits_no_version.finding: At a fixed total sample count, increasing the number of classes reduces survival by a factor k and contamination by √k, reducing their ratio by √k.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this Gaussian-feature multiclass model, fewer positive examples per class weaken the survival/contamination ratio and constrain sufficient conditions for generalization.

record.problems: The result is theoretical and limited to a bi-level Gaussian-feature model with 1-sparse noiseless labels. The main theorem gives sufficient conditions only. The authors state their sufficient conditions are likely loose and present a conjecture for a larger region; there is no empirical evaluation of natural datasets or random-label fitting in this paper.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported empirical result on a V1–V8 intervention or measure was found. Cited deep-network memorization and double-descent results are prior work, not this study's results. The main asymptotic theorem is represented by R1; no individual parameter-sweep outcomes are reported as separate result rows.

untested.parts: No comparison of fixed random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy and random-label held-out accuracy using the same architecture and training recipe.
No neural-network width comparison establishing continued test-error improvement beyond the width needed to interpolate.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD under specified tuning budgets.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurements or comparison of generalization-gap rankings.
No removal of memorized examples and retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The V1 verdicts in the record should be removed. Generalization by an interpolating classifier alone does not establish V1, and class-count sensitivity does not limit its scope. Discussion of the original memorization and width findings supplies background rather than a test.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test memorization of random labels or the stated deep-network architectures and recipes; no numerical held-out accuracy is reported.
Studies asymptotic feature and class scaling for a linear model, not a width sweep of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks or test-error peak near interpolation.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
No sharpness or other trained-network generalization-measure comparison.
No removal or retraining of memorized examples.

rows.subject: minimum-norm interpolating classifier
rows.size_stated: d = floor(n^p); k = c_k floor(n^t); s = floor(n^r)
rows.operation_detail: Asymptotic analysis of misclassification probability under the bi-level ensemble model and 1-sparse noiseless labels.

conditions.value: class is index of largest of first k features; noiseless
favored features weighted according to equations (13)–(14)

rows.value: P(Eerr) → 0 under the stated sufficient conditions
rows.locator: Theorem 5.1, Section 5; restated in Appendix B
rows.note: The result is an asymptotic theorem for a synthetic linear model, not an empirical deep-network result. It establishes a sufficient region only; behavior outside it is not established by the theorem.
rows.check: The theorem is accurately summarized, but it establishes asymptotically vanishing error for a synthetic linear classifier, not V1's random-versus-natural-label comparison or V2's decrease in test error with network width. Joint asymptotic scaling of samples, features, weights and classes does not establish a width effect. The stated conditions are sufficient; failure outside them is not proved.

rows.subject: corresponding regression problem
rows.operation_detail: Compares the classification theorem's parameter regime with the corresponding regression setting.

conditions.value: bi-level model; true class labels generated by largest of first k features

rows.baseline: multiclass classification result in the same parameter regime
rows.value: The corresponding regression problem does not generalize well
rows.note: The regression comparison is stated with reference to prior work; the paper does not provide a new regression experiment here.
rows.check: The regression failure is attributed to Muthukumar et al. [56], so it should not be a standalone result row for this study. Its target is a real-valued linear combination of favored features, not the largest-feature class label listed in the row. Neither regression failure nor the classification comparison tests V1.

rows.subject: binary classification problem
rows.operation_detail: Compares the multiclass setting's survival and contamination behavior with binary classification as the number of classes increases.

conditions.value: same total number of training points; fewer positive examples per class as k increases

rows.value: The overall survival/contamination ratio decreases by a factor of √k
rows.locator: Section 5, discussion following Equation (22); Conclusion, Section 6
rows.note: This is an analytical comparison explaining the multiclass difficulty, not a measurement of random-label memorization or a deep-network held-out error.
rows.check: The analytical 1/√k decline in the survival/contamination ratio concerns increasing class count, not random-label memorization or any other listed version. Calling it partial evidence for V1 is unjustified; the ratio is an explanatory quantity rather than a direct measurement of V1's effect.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
